# October counts: who counted what

Collected 2026-11-13. Machine-readable twin: `data/story/october_counts.json` (status: draft). Fetched with WebFetch, which returns small-model extracts of the page: quotes below are the tool's extracts; "paraphrase" means not quotable. Paywalled sources excluded.

## Verdict on each v2 claim

| # | v2 claim | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 Oct Delhi "500+ reportedly held"; 11 stations close; internet cut near CP before the first protester | **Corrected** | AJ (2 Oct): "Reports about 3pm ... suggested that more than 500 people ... had been arrested in New Delhi", unattributed "reports". Count kept rising: ~150 (official, early) -> ~500 -> 700+ (police) -> nearly 1,000 (police sources, PTI). AJ says "at least 11 metro stations" and does NOT mention internet or Connaught Place. IFF (2 Oct) says "entry and exit at eleven metro stations have been closed" and condemns mobile-internet suspension "in and around Connaught Place"; Jio message at 9:40 am, protest called for 11 am. Credit IFF for internet/CP, not AJ. |
| 2 | 10 Oct Mumbai "more than 600", mobile internet restricted (Amnesty) | **Count confirmed; internet claim unsupported** | Amnesty: "In Mumbai, police detained more than 600 people on 10 October as they tried to gather at August Kranti Maidan." Amnesty mentions mobile-internet restrictions only for the 10-11 Oct weekend generally, no city. Police (PTI) put ~200 at the Maidan and ~600 city-wide; ANI via AJ "some 600 arrested". |
| 3 | 12 Oct Bengaluru "at least 100" (Amnesty) | **Confirmed as Amnesty's, but disputed** | Amnesty: "at least 100 people who were marching towards the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer". South First: "around 50-60 protesters around 3:30 pm on Monday, 12 October". Organiser is My Vote My Right (40+ civil-society groups), not named as CJP in South First or TNM. |
| 4 | "Three city counts ... about 1,200" | **Unsupported, drop** | 500 (Delhi, 2 Oct, early) + 600 (Mumbai, 10 Oct) + 100 (Bengaluru, 12 Oct) adds three different days and claimants, and ignores Delhi 10 Oct (2,000 to 7,000 by police/MHA/media). Delhi 2 Oct alone reached ~1,000 by police sources. |
| 5 | 8 Oct spokesperson "at least 10,000" nationwide; AJ could not verify | **Confirmed** | Claimant is Ashutosh Ranka, CJP spokesperson, X post Thu 8 Oct (name and title from tool summary, asked twice). "Al Jazeera could not immediately verify the claims." A cumulative claim, not a one-day count. |
| 6 | Amnesty: "detained thousands in Delhi" 10-11 Oct | **Confirmed** | Amnesty paraphrase: over the weekend of 10-11 October police detained thousands and restricted access to sites, transport and mobile internet. No number. Snippet: "police detained thousands of protesters and imposed restrictions affecting access to protest sites". |
| 7 | 13-21 Oct: Jantar Mantar struck off; Das and Ranka arrested, remanded, released after 7 days on an undertaking | **Corrected (dates)** | Removal was **12 Oct** (Amnesty: "On 12 October, Delhi Police officially removed Jantar Mantar from the list of legal, permitted areas"), not 13. Arrest 13 Oct (Tue). Remand 14 Oct (Wed) to 5 days. 19 Oct (Mon) extended by 2 days (SEM Ritu Raj, ThePrint). Released 21 Oct after "their 7th day in judicial custody" (BNSS 7-day aggregate cap); police wanted 3 more. Undertaking confirmed by The Logical Indian (ledger). "7 days" = judicial custody; from the 13 Oct arrest it is 8 calendar days. |
| 8 | Aakar Patel quote, 14 Oct | **Confirmed verbatim** | "Authorities cannot use the criminal justice system to punish people for exercising their right to peaceful assembly." Role: Chair of Board, Amnesty International India. |

Free Press Journal: 15,000 police and 25,000 paramilitary deployed (a deployment figure; ignore, not the CJP "15,000").

## Conflicts with epilogue_october.json

1. **10 Oct "about 2,000 to 15,000"** understates the spread. Same-day police/PTI figures reach 3,000 and nearly 7,000. The ledger's range must not read as the full range of claims. The 15,000 is Gulf News, naming Shinde; ledger cites Zee (404 today) and says "about".
2. **Ledger link `reuters`** points at the AJ URL; give it its own source id (`oct_aj_1010`).
3. **16 Oct**: ledger carries ~150 (police) as "disputed" against Fair Observer "more than 100" (7 Nov, undated). The 150 holds (PTI, Tribune, Zee, "so far"). The two are not a real conflict: "more than 100" is compatible with ~150.
4. **Mumbai**: ledger m61 "~600 (ANI)" fine, but the first police count was ~200, then 400, then ~600. Amnesty's 600 is at the Maidan; police say ~200 there.
5. **Bengaluru**: Amnesty at least 100 vs South First 50-60, and the march is My Vote My Right, not CJP-labelled. Apparatus ledger already notes this.
6. **Das/Ranka "7 days"**: epilogue_october.json is right for judicial custody (13 Oct arrest to 21 Oct release is 8 calendar days). The earlier ~24-hour detention of Dipke, Das and Ranka at the airport (10-11 Oct) is a separate episode: do not add it to the 7.
7. Epilogue fact 2026-10-13 gives "14 people (police via Hans India) / about 20 volunteers (AJ)". AJ 19 Oct says "14 protesters who climbed over barricades"; AJ 13 Oct says "about 20 volunteers who 'sneaked' into". AJ contradicts itself across articles.

## Roach-count guidance (not decisions)

- Never sum across cities or claimants. Delhi 10 Oct figures overlap by definition.
- One-roach-per-person is workable only for single claimants: Mumbai 600 (police, PTI) and Delhi 16 Oct 150 (police) are safe. For Delhi 10 Oct show the claimants side by side (about 2,000 MHA/Reuters; nearly 2,500 The Hindu/police sources; more than 3,000 PTI; nearly 7,000 PTI/FPJ; more than 15,000 CJP).
- 600 preventive detentions of people with criminal records are a separate police category.

## Fetch failures and limits

- CNN (HTTP 451), Zee News 7,000/15,000 article (404), Zee CJP-leaders-released (404), Deccan Herald 3,000 (403), The Statesman (403): not read. Reuters.com blocked; Reuters figures only via AJ and a live blog. The Hindu 2,500 not located; only via AJ.
- WebFetch returns model-written extracts, so verbatim quotes are only as reliable as the tool; all quoted snippets were extracted, not eyeballed. Amnesty paragraphs on Mumbai/Bengaluru returned as paraphrase with quoted fragments.
- Search results (also summarised) were used only to find URLs; every count in the table was read on its own page, except those marked second-hand.
- I did not find per-city or cumulative October totals from CJP, Amnesty or police beyond those listed. No police statement with a single official cumulative total was found.
